bug_semantics: With createUserDir enabled and the CLI-default user scope set to '.', hook- and proxy-auth auto-provisioning copied that nonempty default into the new user and passed it unchanged to Settings.MakeUserDir. MakeUserDir derives /users/<username> only when the incoming scope is empty; for '.', path.Join('/', '.') instead produces '/', so every externally provisioned user was persisted with the server-root scope and could read, modify, share, or delete other users' files.
flaw_origin: The smallest mainline-history commit that first wrote the flawed mechanism is dda9a389f387e94643a9a2ae56027260b210152a. It added auth/hook.go and, in HookAuth.SaveUser at introduced lines 158-179, initialized Scope from a.Settings.Defaults.Scope and called MakeUserDir with that inherited scope without the scope-clearing step already required for createUserDir isolation. The analogous proxy missing-user provisioning path was added later by 209acf2429b06e2e8d78218937c59fd7e7edd1be; it is a second manifestation, not the first BIC.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Ramires Viana <59319979+ramiresviana@users.noreply.github.com> and committer Oleg Lobanov <oleg@lobanov.me>; its complete message is 'feat: hook authentication method' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-j7jh-37pf-mf8h and its repository API record https://api.github.com/repos/filebrowser/filebrowser/security-advisories/GHSA-j7jh-37pf-mf8h identify CVE-2026-72837, auth/hook.go, auth/proxy.go, settings/dir.go, and the exact '.' -> '/' mechanism; the current structured range is <=2.63.19 with patched version 2.63.20. Source history: git log -L :SaveUser:auth/hook.go and git log -S'MakeUserDir(u.Username, u.Scope' -- auth/hook.go both trace the vulnerable hook call to dda9a389f387e94643a9a2ae56027260b210152a (https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/commit/dda9a389f387e94643a9a2ae56027260b210152a). At that tree, auth/hook.go:158-179 sets Scope at line 161 from a.Settings.Defaults.Scope, calls MakeUserDir at line 172, assigns the result at line 176, and saves it at line 179; settings/dir.go:23-33 derives a username home only for an empty scope and otherwise normalizes with path.Join('/', userScope), while cmd/root.go:319-320 supplies the default Scope '.'. Direct-parent verification: git cat-file -e f80b016ef0e169f578bd23dd7916cf80c6b7a31d:auth/hook.go fails because the file does not exist, and git grep for HookAuth and the vulnerable MakeUserDir call in that parent has no match; git diff-tree marks auth/hook.go as added by the BIC. The BIC is a one-parent member commit, not a squash aggregate, and v2.23.0 is the first tag containing it. The later proxy manifestation is 209acf2429b06e2e8d78218937c59fd7e7edd1be, first contained by v2.32.0, matching the advisory's proxy-history boundary. Direct fix 8ddd3d1db9b9f5727d0bf96ea0e7d9a25a8692b4 (https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/commit/8ddd3d1db9b9f5727d0bf96ea0e7d9a25a8692b4) adds settings.CreateUserHome at settings/dir.go:45-76, clears user.Scope at lines 55-57 when derivation is required, and routes both auth/hook.go:160-168 and auth/proxy.go:53-57 through it; it is absent from v2.63.18 and first appears in v2.63.19. The advisory prose says the root-scope flaw was fixed in v2.63.19, but its current structured metadata designates 2.63.20 as patched; final boundary commit fb6aeba9eae7b8eb401e0db325973781e1ffd08b (https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/commit/fb6aeba9eae7b8eb401e0db325973781e1ffd08b) makes the associated provisioned-scope collision check atomic and is first contained by v2.63.20. Exact BIC-object inspection with git cat-file commit dda9a389f387e94643a9a2ae56027260b210152a yielded the human author/committer and no trailers or AI marker.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle starts with the hook feature's own smallest member commit, not with a later move, blame survivor, proxy replication, merge, or release commit. dda9a389f387e94643a9a2ae56027260b210152a introduced the complete new-user hook path whose two coupled choices—inherit the nonempty default scope and call MakeUserDir without clearing it—made createUserDir ineffective. Its direct parent has neither auth/hook.go nor an equivalent HookAuth path, proving parent-tree absence. The BIC is already present in v2.23.0; 209acf2429b06e2e8d78218937c59fd7e7edd1be later copied the same causal error into proxy auto-provisioning for v2.32.0. The direct corrective commit 8ddd3d1db9b9f5727d0bf96ea0e7d9a25a8692b4 centralizes creation, empties non-explicit scopes before MakeUserDir, preserves an explicit trusted hook scope, and is in v2.63.19; fb6aeba9eae7b8eb401e0db325973781e1ffd08b completes the advisory's current 2.63.20 patched boundary by making its related derived-scope ownership check atomic. Thus both the exact flaw fix and the published fixed-version boundary are tied to full commits. Finally, attribution is based only on the dda9a389f387e94643a9a2ae56027260b210152a commit object: it records human author and committer identities and no AI marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
